description: Governorships elected in presidential years. Nine states elect governors to four-year terms in presidential years; New Hampshire and Vermont elect every two years, so they vote in every cycle. The same eleven states vote in 2028, 2032 and 2036.

sources.name: Wikipedia — 2028 United States gubernatorial elections (11 states; election day November 7, 2028; NH and VT two-year terms)
National Governors Association — Governors' terms and term limits
sources.note: Term lengths: four years everywhere except New Hampshire and Vermont (two years).

notes: The brief expected 11 presidential-year governor races; confirmed: DE, IN, MO, MT, NH, NC, ND, UT, VT, WA, WV.
Puerto Rico and American Samoa also elect governors in presidential years; territories are out of scope.
Incumbents are as of 2026-10-06 and informational only. NH and VT hold elections on 2026-11-03, so their 2028 incumbents are unknown.

Vermont: Vt. Const. ch. II, § 47 — if no candidate has a majority, the General Assembly elects the governor from the top three by joint ballot in January. The market resolves to the party of whoever is finally elected by that process.
Washington: top-two general election (two candidates advance from the August primary; the general is decided by plurality of the two).
No presidential-year governor race has a general-election runoff.

states.note: Has said he will not run in 2028.
Two-year term; also elected 2026-11-03. General Assembly chooses if no majority.
Eligible to run again. Top-two general.
